Posted on November 15, 2026 by steve blank Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang had resigned 33 years after he co-founded the company. What happens to a company when a visionary CEO is gone? Most often innovation dies and the company coasts for years on momentum and its brand. Rarely does it regain its former glory. That’s the danger facing Nvidia. Here’s what their board should be considering. Here’s why. Jensen Huang reinvented Nvidia three times. In 2006 he launched CUDA , turning a graphics chip for PC gamers into a general-purpose computing platform – and funded it for years ahead of any revenue. In 2012, when researchers used Nvidia chips to win the ImageNet contest , he pointed the company to deep learning. In 2020, with the acquisition of Mellanox , Nvidia went from selling boards with GPUs to selling integrated racks that power AI datacenters. These were not just product transitions, but radical business model transitions; new channels, new customers and new markets. Nvidia pivoted from a vendor of graphics boards, to a software platform, and then to systems company. It’s hard to imagine a CEO focused on executing an existing business model funding CUDA through those years. Steve Jobs did the same at Apple, transforming it from a niche computer company into the most profitable company in the world. Between 2001 and 2008, Jobs reinvented the company three times. Visionary CEOs are not “just” great at assuring world-class execution of a successful business model, they are also world-class innovators . The best are agile and know how to pivot, making substantive changes to their business model while or before their market has shifted. The very best of them shape markets – they know how to create new markets by seeing opportunities before anyone else . They remain entrepreneurs . Visionary CEOs don’t need someone else to demo the company’s key products for them. They deeply understand products, and they have their own coherent and consistent vision of where the industry/business models and customers are today, and where they need to take the company. They know who their customers are because they spend time talking to them. They use strategy committees and the exec staff for advice, but none of these CEOs pivot by committee . Microsoft and Apple are two examples of what happens when a visionary CEO is replaced by an execution CEO. Microsoft and the Cost of Missing the Next Market Microsoft entered the 21st century as the dominant software provider for anyone who interacted with a computing device. After running Microsoft for 25 years, Bill Gates handed the reins of Microsoft to Steve Ballmer in January 2000. Ballmer went on to run Microsoft for the next 14 years. Ballmer organized the company around execution of its then current strengths – Windows and Office businesses. He tripled Microsoft’s sales to $78 billion and profits more than doubled from $9 billion to $22 billion, but those results hid missed opportunities that would reshape computing. Ballmer failed to understand and execute on the five most important technology trends of the 21st century: in search – losing to Google; in smartphones – losing to Apple; in mobile operating systems – losing to Google/Apple; in media – losing to Apple/Netflix; and in the cloud – losing to Amazon. In early 2014, Satya Nadella took charge. Nadella got Microsoft organized around the cloud (Azure), freed the Office and Azure teams from Windows and killed the phone business. Nadella saved Microsoft from irrelevance. Today Microsoft is worth about $4 trillion . It is one of the few companies that regained its former glory, after its board replaced a salesman with a product and engineering insider. Innovation CEOs Hire Execution VPs Successful visionary CEOs build an executive staff of world-class operating executives and technical leaders (and they unconsciously force out any world-class innovators from their direct reports). The problem is in a company driven by a visionary CEO; there is only one visionary. Nvidia is the extreme case. Jensen had about 60 direct reports and discouraged one-on-one meetings. No long-term plans. Much like Jobs, he made himself the point where technical, product and business decisions came together. Replacing that role is harder than filling a box on an organization chart. He said he didn’t believe in succession planning . When visionary founders depart (resignation, death, firing, etc.), their operating executives believe it’s their turn to run the company. At Microsoft, Bill Gates chose Steve Ballmer, and at Apple Steve Jobs chose Tim Cook. Jensen anointed no one. Once in charge, one of the first things these operations/execution CEOs do is to get rid of the chaos and turbulence in the organization. Execution CEOs value stability, process and repeatable execution. On one hand that’s great for predictability, but it often starts a creative death spiral – creative people start to leave, and other executors (without the innovation talent of the old leader) are put into more senior roles – hiring more process people, which in turn forces out the remaining creative talent. This culture shift ripples down from the top and what once felt like a company on a mission to change the world now feels like another job . (Amazon is a counterexample. Before succeeding Jeff Bezos, Andy Jassy had already founded and led AWS . He was an innovator who had built a new business inside the existing company.) At Nvidia this step isn’t optional. No one else can run a company with 60 direct reports, so the next CEO’s first move will be to add layers of management. Why Tim Cook Was the New Steve Ballmer Tim Cook ran Apple for 15 years. Apple under Cook grew its revenues from $108 billion to $416 billion and its market value from $350 billion to about $4 trillion. The iPhone continued its annual upgrades of incremental improvements. The transition to Apple silicon showed that major technical change on the chip level was possible under his leadership. But Apple silicon was a better engine for the existing products Apple already had, not a new market. Apple stumbled badly on the one major product category launched under Cook – Apple Vision Pro and missed badly on AI (Siri was actually first with a Chatbot.) This year it turned to Google to help fix Siri. In September 2026 Cook handed the job to John Ternus. How Nvidia Could Miss the Boat The threat to Nvidia is already visible: its biggest customers are becoming its competitors. Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI and Tesla are all building their own AI chips . Jensen’s answer was to keep innovating and bring to market a new generation of chips every year, build a moat around an integrated hardware and software platform ( CUDA ), and invest ~$50 billion in the AI labs that run on Nvidia. It’s likely these are the bets an execution CEO trims first. The irony is that in the 21st century, the tighter you hold on to your current product/markets, the likelier you will be disrupted . The rapid change of technology will create new disruptions that will force “bet the company” decisions about product direction, markets, pricing, supply chain, operations and the reorganization necessary to execute a new business model. In the GPU market, the difference between market dominance and Chapter 11 may be a hands-on product/customer, and business model-centric CEO with an entrepreneurial vision of the future. Four Challenges for the Board of Directors The dilemma facing the board at Nvidia or any board of directors on the departure of an innovative CEO is strategic : Do we still want to be an innovative, risk taking company? Or should we now focus on execution of our core business, reduce our risky bets and maximize shareholder return. Ultimately a board would like both – preserving the speed and ambition of Jensen’s decision-making while distributing enough authority for the company to function without him. Tactically , that question results in asking: Do you search for another innovator from outside, promote one of the executors or go deeper down the organization to find an innovator? Herein lies four challenges. Steve Jobs and Bill Gates chose execution executives as their successors. The result was they confused world-class execution with the passion for product and customers, and market insight. From the perspective of Gates there was no difference between him and Ballmer and Jobs believed Cook could be equally creative. Yet history has shown they were world-class stewards of a business model each had been handed. Yet long-term survival in markets that change rapidly require innovation and execution.. Nvidia’s board has a different version of this problem. Jensen suggested no one, and he left the board the day he left the job. The decision belongs to a board in crisis, led by the first chair the company has ever had. Boards in crisis reach for stability. That gets you an execution CEO by a different road. Nvidia’s board should ask what its candidates have built under uncertainty. If the board decides that the company needs another innovator at the helm, you can almost guarantee that the best executor – the number 2 and/or 3 vice president in the company – will leave, feeling that they deserved the job. Now the board is faced with not only having lost its CEO, but potentially the best of the executive staff. Many innovative/visionary CEOs have become part of the company’s brand. Steve Jobs, Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk and Jensen Huang. This isn’t a new phenomenon, think of 20th-century icons like Walt Disney, Edwin Land at Polaroid and Henry Ford. But they’re not only an external face to the company, they were often the touchstone for internal decision-making. Years after a visionary CEO is gone, companies are still asking, “What would Walt Disney/Steve Jobs/Henry Ford have done?” rather than figuring out what they should now be doing in the changing market. Jensen was more than the brand. He set Nvidia’s foreign policy, and was the company’s face in Washington, Beijing and Taipei. No Nvidia operating VP has done that job. The next Nvidia CEO inherits a Congress and investigators asking how many restricted Nvidia chips reached China. As companies grow larger and management falls prey to the fallacy that it only exists to maximize shareholder short-term return on investment, companies become risk averse. Large companies and their boards live in fear of losing what they spent years gaining (customers, market share, revenue, profits.) This may work in stable markets and technologies. But today very few of those remain. And certainly not Nvidia’s market. Lessons Learned Nvidia’s order book and CUDA will make the next two or three years look fine no matter who is CEO (unless a meaningful share of that revenue turns out to be chips that were diverted to China .) Innovation CEOs are almost always replaced by one of their execution VPs If they have inherited a powerful business model (like Nvidia) this often results in gains in revenue and profits that can continue for years However, as soon as the market, business model, technology shifts, these execution CEOs are ill-equipped to deal with the change The result is a company obsoleted by more agile competitors and their company is left to live off momentum in its twilight years Nvidia’s board has to decide what it is hiring its next CEO to do. Executing today’s business is essential. So is reinventing it before someone else makes it obsolete. title: Nvidia was in trouble before the Jensen Huang mess
body_text: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess | WIRED Skip to main content THE WIRED APP IS HERE DOWNLOAD NOW » Menu WIRED SECURITY POLITICS THE BIG STORY BUSINESS SCIENCE CULTURE REVIEWS Menu WIRED Account Account Newsletters Security Politics The Big Story Business Science Culture Reviews Chevron More Expand The Big Interview Magazine Events WIRED Insider WIRED Consulting Newsletters Podcasts Video Livestreams WIRED Store Search Search Will Knight Business Nov 16, 2026 6:00 AM Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos. Photo-Illustration: Wired Staff; Getty Images Comment Loader Save Story Save this story Comment Loader Save Story Save this story Nvidia played a key role enabling the AI gold rush thanks in large part to its recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang . Huang was a master of foreseeing technological changes , investing in chips to train AI earlier than most. But just as he’s leaving , the company has a growing list of competitors with a range of new, advanced technology breathing down its neck. For Nvidia , where CFO Colette Kress has now taken the reins, the timing isn’t great. “Everything sold today was designed two to three years ago,” says the CEO of a large AI company, who spoke to WIRED on condition of anonymity to avoid hurting business relationships. Kress, or whoever replaces her permanently, will have to chart the course that the chip industry will take two years from now, the CEO says. Already, competitors have started to move in. Nvidia dominates the market for AI accelerators, capturing 80 percent of sales, according to Silicon Analysis. Longtime nemesis AMD is now making a concerted effort to build competitive AI chips. Its share of the market has crept up from just two percent in 2022 to between 7 and 10 percent in 2026. Big US cloud players—Google, Amazon, and Microsoft—are all developing more specialized chips to power the training and serving of AI models. Each has seen similar gains. These companies are designing their own silicon to reduce costs and to gain some independence from Nvidia. Several startups now offer more specialized chips that promise improvements over Nvidia’s core products. Cerebras, for instance, sells giant ones meant to power giant AI models. AMD recently bought Taalas, a company that burns models’ weights into silicon to make computations ultra efficient. Using these chips requires rewriting a lot of code, however, to make them work with cutting-edge AI models. Patrick Moorhead, chief analyst at MoorInStrat, a company that tracks the chip industry, says the rise of AI agents makes inference, or running models that have already been trained, more important. That’s an area where Nvidia has less of an edge compared to cloud hyperscalers and startups. Nvidia did, however, acquire a startup making specialized chips, called Groq, in December of 2025. And because of the rise in AI assistants and agents, there’s also growing demand for general purpose central processing units (CPUs), Moorhead said, an area where Nvidia barely competes. Nvidia still maintains a huge lead in AI thanks to Huang’s foresight. Huang cofounded the company in 1993 to design graphics chips for PCs. In the mid-2010s, he saw the promise of AI. He funded academic research on the topic, developed software to support AI engineering, and gave hardware to labs and startups. In 2022, ChatGPT took AI mainstream and sales of Nvidia chips skyrocketed. The company’s revenue went from $26.91 billion in January 2022 to $215.94 billion in January 2026. The challenges it faces may not be existential—but they do add up, especially on a global scale. China Challenge While Nvidia’s fortunes have risen in the US, they have declined in the world’s other big market for AI: China. Washington is trying to restrict access to its most advanced chips, while Beijing is trying to develop its own chip industry. Nvidia is not allowed to sell its most powerful chips in China, but it can sell previous generations. Sales of these chips as well as non AI chips doubled over the past year, but China now accounts for only eight percent of the company’s overall revenue, compared with 20 percent in 2024, according to its fillings. It remains unclear how many chips exported to other countries may either end up in China or end up being used remotely by Chinese firms. Huawei, a Chinese tech giant targeted with US sanctions for several years, has developed new kinds of supercomputers that harness many more chips than usual to train and run AI models. Some Chinese AI companies, such as Z.ai, which makes one of the world’s best open source models, say they’ve trained their models entirely using Huawei’s chips. If Chinese open-weight models gain traction in other countries, it could create a market for Chinese chips elsewhere. Huang’s dealings with China played a major role in his downfall. He had a romantic relationship with Huang Le, also known as Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at a Singaporean company called Megaspeed who the US government suspects of being an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed and its subsidiaries have reportedly imported between $4.6 and $7.5 billion Nvidia chips into southeast Asia. Reports suggest that the company may have provided access to the chips to Chinese AI firms. Babak Minovi, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, a consultancy that focuses on technology and geopolitics, says Huang was right to point out that cutting off access to China would empower domestic rivals. “Huang was taking a pragmatic line, and he knows competition,” he says. Trend Spotting Even in markets that it dominates, Nvidia may turn out to be a victim of its own success. The AI models built using Nvidia’s chip are automating the very elements of coding, data analysis, and scientific research that help design chips. Most chip design firms use specialized AI models to arrange components on processors—something that traditionally required deep engineering expertise and experience. And both OpenAI and Anthropic have recently touted the ability of their newest models to design electronics from scratch. Moorhead says the shift towards AI chip design may not pose a huge threat to Nvidia because it’s riding the same wave. “They have access to AI too,” he notes. But Moorhead says the way AI models can now quickly rewrite code to run on different hardware may prove a problem. For years, Nvidia has attracted developers by providing software that makes it easy to write programs and build models for its silicon. Its Compute Unified Device Architecture, or CUDA, has long been seen as a moat to ensure AI companies continue to rely on Nvidia chips. But AI models are now so good at reading and writing code that they can port an AI model over to a competitor's silicon at speed. Wafer, a startup that uses AI to port models to AMD and then serves them more cheaply, has seen revenue grow spectacularly in recent months, boasts CEO Emilio Andere. Every time a major new open weight model is released Wafer can have it running on AMD hardware at least 80 percent as efficiently within hours, he says. Andere says AI is getting so capable that his engineers barely have to edit or review the code. Dan Hutchinson, a veteran chip analyst, says Nvidia may be entering its “Intel swan moment,” referring to the 2019 replacement of engineering-focused CEO Brian Krzanich with its CFO Bob Swan. ( Sound familiar ? Krzanich also resigned after a relationship with an employee; Huang is alleged to have had multiple.) From there, the company’s focus shifted to sales more than technical progress. Bureaucracy ballooned and revenue tanked. “Nvidia is now an Intel waiting to happen,” he says. title: Lovable apps expose passport details and more than 200K private messages
body_text: Lovable: Many Apps Expose Sensitive Data — Crissy Field GmbH Home Anwendungssicherheit Beratung Softwareentwicklung Case Studies Research Ãber uns < All Research Reports (German) Lovable: Many Apps Built on the Platform Expose Sensitive Data AI makes it easier to build your own web applications, but handling sensitive data still requires special care. We examined 159,041 Lovable projects and found many cases where personal and confidential information was accessible without logging in. Diesen Artikel auf Deutsch lesen About Lovable Lovable is a Swedish AI startup founded in Stockholm in 2023 by Anton Osika and Fabian Hedin. The platform turns plain-language descriptions into web applications and is designed to be accessible even to people with little or no programming experience . Lovable grew out of Osika’s open-source project “GPT Engineer”, released in 2023. The project evolved into the GPT Engineer App before being renamed Lovable in late 2024 and launching publicly that November. Visit the Lovable website The Promise Lovable can build impressively sophisticated web projects with AI, from static websites to full applications with user management and database connections. But as soon as an application handles confidential information, one question becomes crucial: Is that data protected against unauthorized access? In its marketing , Lovable repeatedly emphasizes that no technical knowledge is needed to build projects . This can give the impression that the platform takes care of security too. Yet Lovable’s Terms & Conditions place responsibility for applications and data handling on the customers themselves. That leaves a troubling gap between the promise of an easy-to-use, all-in-one service and the responsibilities customers are expected to take on. Against this backdrop, we investigated how well sensitive data in Lovable applications is protected, in collaboration with Handelsblatt . Lina Knees reported on the findings on November 2, 2026 (in German) . Research Question We wanted to find out whether sensitive data in Lovable applications was accessible without logging in. We looked separately at data sent when a website first loaded and additional content we checked by making further read-only requests with the same API key. The result: We found many clear examples of sensitive data left unprotected. Methodology We focused on the database service Supabase . Its integration is relatively easy to analyze, and we believe it is the most widely used database service among Lovable projects. Lovable’s own database features, introduced in late 2025, are still less widely used. Similar misconfigurations may occur there too, but we did not examine them in this analysis. Using datasets from the open web archive Common Crawl , we identified and analyzed 159,041 Lovable projects from December 2025 to September 2026 . Of these, 34,545 used Supabase. 24,664 websites sent database records from Supabase as soon as they loaded, without requiring a login or any other interaction. That alone is not a security issue: the data may be intended for public display. But by making additional read-only requests, we were able to retrieve more database content. We found records containing email addresses in 10,560 tables across 7,403 of the 24,664 websites (30%). Limitations Email addresses can help identify records containing personal data, but they may also be public contact addresses or test data. At the same time, this approach misses personal records that contain no email address. These effects partly offset one another, though we could not establish to what extent. The 30% figure should therefore not be read as a confirmed data leak rate. It applies only to the 24,664 websites we examined more closely. Our sample, drawn from Common Crawl, is also not representative of all Lovable applications. We retrieved only parts of the datasets rather than downloading them in full. The figures below reflect the records we actually downloaded; the affected datasets may contain more. We are not publishing details of how to access them, as doing so could make further access easier. Data Leaks We found many serious cases of exposed data, including: A German lifestyle forum exposed more than 80,000 profiles containing full names, email addresses, dates of birth, and gender information. More than 200,000 chat messages were also accessible. Several event organizers and restaurants exposed tens of thousands of records relating to ticket and food sales , with no login required. The records we inspected included email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses, payment information, and ticket codes. A property management company exposed AI-generated summaries of internal emails containing sensitive information about tenants, property owners, and business partners. In a particularly serious case, a service provider exposed more than 1,000 records containing identity document details , including passport numbers , expiration dates , and nationalities . These highly sensitive identity details could be used for identity theft. Other accessible content included tens of thousands of contracts , invoices , personal photo albums , and internal WhatsApp communications . We also found numerous newsletter subscriptions, waiting lists, and contact and support inquiries. In one case, 280,000 emails sent to a provider’s customers were accessible. Depending on what it contains, exposed data like this could be used for phishing, ticket fraud, or identity theft. We could not establish whether any of it had been misused. Handelsblatt contacted Lovable with the findings of our investigation. Implications Our analysis shows that many Lovable applications leave even highly sensitive data unprotected, with potentially serious consequences for the people affected. Access control mistakes can happen in any application, whether written by people or built with AI. With Lovable, database integrations follow recurring patterns, making it easier for attackers to look for similar misconfigurations across many applications. An approach that works against one app may then work against others with little extra effort. Users without a technical background also face a harder task spotting and preventing these flaws. An easy-to-use development platform does not remove the need for an expert review of access permissions before an application handles confidential data. Automated checks are no substitute for a professional security assessment . Before an application handles real customer or business data, its access permissions, interfaces, and separation between user accounts should be reviewed. These checks should be repeated after significant changes. If the necessary expertise is not available in-house, bring in qualified support. If you would like help securing your application, please get in touch. Note: This research report presents a more recent analysis and updated figures compared with the Handelsblatt article published on November 2, 2026. title: Old Bitly links are being hijacked
body_text: Old Bitly links hijacked in Burger King, McDonald’s and Trump tweets | Ransomnews Close Menu Home News Security Privacy Cybercrime Threat Groups Ransomware Explainers Stealer Logs AI OSINT Tools Ransomtracker Ransomware attacks today Stealercheck FortiBleed Checker Site Check Data Ransomware statistics Ransom payment rate Breach verification Infostealer statistics Newsletter About Us Facebook X (Twitter) Instagram Threads Ransomnews Home News Security Privacy Cybercrime Threat Groups Ransomware Explainers Stealer Logs AI OSINT Tools Ransomtracker Ransomware attacks today Stealercheck FortiBleed Checker Site Check Data Ransomware statistics Ransom payment rate Breach verification Infostealer statistics Newsletter About Us Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Ransomnews Security Old Bitly links hijacked in Burger King, McDonald’s and Trump tweets By Ransomnews Research Team November 15, 2026 Updated: November 15, 2026 No Comments 21 Mins Read 27,336 Views Share Facebook Twitter Pinterest LinkedIn Tumblr Email Copy Link Share Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Email Copy Link Update, 15 November, 23:40 UTC: CNN reports redirected Bitly links in old posts from Bill Gates, Justin Trudeau, Mike Pence, the FBI and the US Department of Defense as well. Our third check of the Trump links, at 23:35 UTC, found nothing new: 49 links re-created years after their tweets still work. Update, 15 November, 22:30 UTC: Bitly has confirmed the problem. In a post on X at 19:13 UTC it said it had identified an issue that “allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links” and send people to unrelated content. Bitly said it has suspended the accounts involved and is disabling the affected links. It added that its Trust and Safety team is working on protections against similar misuse. Earlier today, we identified an issue that allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links to redirect people to content unrelated to the original posts. We have suspended the accounts involved and are disabling the affected links. Our Trust and Safety team is working… — Bitly (@Bitly) November 15, 2026 Update, 15 November, 19:30 UTC: The Burger King and McDonald’s links no longer redirect. Both were still working at 15:05 UTC and returned Bitly’s “Link Deactivated” page by 19:22 UTC. The same has happened to the two extra Trump links we verified and to six of the seven links in our sample that pointed somewhere new. The seventh now shows a Bitly warning that the account that created it has been suspended. The 49 re-created links that look like the originals still work. Burger King’s X account was not hacked. A Bitly short link in a tweet the chain posted on 24 July 2011 was registered again by someone else on 15 November 2026 and pointed at Wikipedia’s list of Nazi concentration camps. The tweet was advertising a restaurant locator. A post quoting it passed 2 million views within hours, and Burger King’s original has since become unavailable. It was not the only one. Eighteen minutes earlier a Bitly link in a McDonald’s tweet from 7 June 2011 was registered the same way and pointed at Wikipedia’s article on the September 11 attacks. Ransomnews also checked 97 Bitly links in Donald Trump’s tweets from 2009 to 2013, taken from a public archive. Bitly’s own link pages show that 56 were created after the tweets they sit in, and a 57th is blocked by Bitly as malicious or spam. Four were registered on 15 November. Two more, created in January 2024 and January 2025, point at domains that copy the names of crypto services. In brief Burger King posted the tweet on 24 July 2011 with the short link bit[.]ly/19BFiM. Bitly’s information page for that link gives a creation time of 05:32 UTC on 15 November 2026 and a destination on Wikipedia. A link in a McDonald’s tweet from 7 June 2011, bit[.]ly/mLWJO0, was created again at 05:14 UTC the same morning, 18 minutes before Burger King’s. It opens Wikipedia’s article on the September 11 attacks. Both tweets have since become unavailable. Nobody posted from either company’s account. The links changed hands on Bitly’s side, so the old tweets send readers wherever the new owners choose. Of 97 Bitly links in Donald Trump’s tweets from 2009 to 2013, 40 are still the original. Another 49 were created again later but lead where the tweets suggest, 48 of them in a 17-minute run on 26 May 2023. Seven lead somewhere else and one is blocked by Bitly. Four of those seven were registered on 15 November 2026 between 07:49 and 09:57 UTC. They open a Roblox profile, a YouTube video (twice) and a Wikipedia article about Trump and Jeffrey Epstein. One Trump tweet from April 2011 carries three links to videos of his children. All three have been replaced. Bitly’s help pages say the ending of a bit.ly link cannot be reused, even after the account behind it is deleted. In February 2025 it was reported to have fixed a bug that allowed this. We found no public statement from Bitly, Burger King or McDonald’s by 14:30 UTC on 15 November. By 19:22 UTC both links returned Bitly’s “Link Deactivated” page. None of the seven Trump links that pointed somewhere new redirects any more. Bitly confirmed the issue on X at 19:13 UTC. It said it has suspended the accounts involved and is disabling the affected links. CNN reported the same evening that old posts from Bill Gates, Justin Trudeau, Mike Pence, the FBI and the US Department of Defense were affected too. We have not checked those links ourselves. Was Burger King hacked? No. Nothing was posted from Burger King’s account and nothing suggests anyone got into it. The tweet is 15 years old and reads as it always did, pointing followers to “our handy restaurant locator” through a Bitly link. What changed is where that link goes. As with the Microsoft 365 outage three days earlier, the first question people asked was whether it was an attack on the company, and the answer is the same. Bitly keeps a public information page for every short link. Add a plus sign to the end of the address and it shows where the link points and when it was created. For bit[.]ly/19BFiM that page gives the destination as Wikipedia’s “List of Nazi concentration camps” and the creation time as 15 November 2026, 05:32 UTC. A link printed in a tweet from 2011 can only carry a 2026 creation date if the same ending was issued a second time. We tested the method on links nobody disputes. A link whose creator says he made it in 2009 shows a 2009 creation date. A custom link tweeted by a YouTube channel on 21 June 2017 shows 20 June 2017. Among the Trump links that are still original, 32 of 40 were created on the day of the tweet or the day before. Burger King’s 2011 tweet as it appeared on the morning of 15 November 2026, quoted by another user. Screenshot: X. The post that spread it came from an X user at 06:51 UTC, 79 minutes after the link was created, and had 2.2 million views by early afternoon. OH LORD https://t.co/QlferLVmNL pic.twitter.com/sk6ceitzXd — The Wizard 🐧 (@42069volshebnik) November 15, 2026 By 13:45 UTC the Burger King post inside it was showing as unavailable. We do not know whether Burger King removed it or X did. The short link was still redirecting to Wikipedia at 13:47 UTC. Was McDonald’s hacked? No. Its link was changed 18 minutes before Burger King’s. On 7 June 2011 McDonald’s tweeted a Bitly link to something its team in Sweden had done. Bitly’s information page for bit[.]ly/mLWJO0 shows the link was created at 05:14 UTC on 15 November 2026, and it redirects to Wikipedia’s article on the September 11 attacks. The tweet was returning a not-found error when we checked at 14:20 UTC. The two changes are close in time and alike in style. The X user Alex Greenland, who spotted both timestamps, thinks one person or group is probably behind them. Nothing we have seen proves that. This Burger King Bitly link was changed at 05:32 UK time today (15 Nov 2026), which is very close to the change of McDonald's tweet Bitly link at 05:14 today. This means it is likely the same actor or group of actors is making these changes. https://t.co/2gqoms5veu pic.twitter.com/u4OxXaPkn2 — Alex Greenland (@ajrgd) November 15, 2026 How does an old Bitly link get hijacked? Someone registers its ending again. The part of a Bitly link after the slash is called the back-half. Bitly generates one at random, or the user types a custom one. If an old link stops existing and its back-half can be claimed, whoever claims it decides where every tweet, email, PDF and printed QR code carrying that link now leads. No password is stolen and no account is touched, so the brand that posted the link sees nothing wrong. Bitly says this cannot happen. Its help page on deleted accounts states that bit.ly links keep working and that their back-halves “cannot be re-used”, whether they were generated or custom. A separate page says Bitly deletes accounts that have been inactive for three years. The creation dates we collected do not fit the first statement. Back-halves that appear in tweets from 2009 to 2012 belong to links created between 2023 and today. It has happened before. In February 2025 Disruptionist reported that memecoin promoters had taken over Bitly links in 2013 posts by Donald Trump and Melania Trump and pointed them at token listings. According to that report, a bug let people claim a back-half once the original link or its account had been deleted or deactivated, and Bitly fixed it and switched off the hijacked links. Links created on 15 November 2026 show the same thing is possible now. The X user Damin Toell identified it as link hijacking at 07:25 UTC and noted that old Trump posts were affected too. Someone is hijacking old bitly links. A lot of this going on with old Trump posts, too. https://t.co/BB5c5BnlFV pic.twitter.com/7JiBxWbirZ — Damin Toell (@damintoell) November 15, 2026 At 09:18 UTC another user described the method in a post that has been viewed more than 46,000 times. Three more Trump links were registered in the 40 minutes that followed. Free tool How does your own site score? Run the same forty passive checks against your own domain: TLS and certificates, security headers, SPF and DMARC, cookies before consent, and what your stack quietly reveals. A grade out of 100 in about fifteen seconds. Your domain Check site No signup. Nothing installed. We only request what your site already serves publicly. How many old links have been replaced? More than half of the ones we tested. We took every tweet Donald Trump’s account posted from 2009 to 2016 from the Trump Twitter Archive data set on GitHub, left out retweets and extracted the bit.ly links. That gave 97 different links, first used between 2009 and 2013, with 61 of them from 2011. We chose this account because its old posts were named in the reports of 15 November and in the 2025 case, and because a full public archive exists. For each link we recorded where it redirects and the creation date on Bitly’s information page, at about 13:45 UTC on 15 November 2026. 57 of 97 Bitly links in old Trump tweets are no longer the original Bitly links in @realDonaldTrump tweets from 2009 to 2013, by what the link is today. Checked on 15 November 2026. Created again, leads where the tweet suggests 49 Still the original link 40 Created again, leads somewhere else 7 Blocked by Bitly 1 Source: Ransomnews check of Bitly link information pages. Tweets from the Trump Twitter Archive data set. Forty links are untouched. Forty-nine were created again later and lead to addresses that fit the tweets: mostly videos on Trump’s YouTube channel, plus pages at CNBC, CNN and the Wall Street Journal. Forty-eight of those were created between 14:55 and 15:12 UTC on 26 May 2023, roughly one every 20 seconds. We do not know who did that. It looks like a repair job by someone who knew where each link used to go, and it means those back-halves were free to claim by May 2023. That leaves eight links that now lead somewhere their tweets never pointed. Tweet date What the tweet promoted Link created again Where it goes now 3 Jun 2009 An iGoogle page 15 Nov 2026, 07:49 UTC A Roblox user profile 1 Jul 2010 A golf course in Scotland 15 Nov 2026, 09:36 UTC A YouTube video 17 Sep 2010 A QVC jewellery show 15 Nov 2026, 09:47 UTC The same YouTube video 7 Oct 2010 A golf course in Scotland 15 Nov 2026, 09:57 UTC Wikipedia’s article on Trump and Jeffrey Epstein 14 Mar 2011 A video blog 29 Jan 2025, 21:09 UTC test[.]com 25 Apr 2011 A video of Donald Trump Jr. 18 Jan 2025, 21:43 UTC worldlibertyfinancial-ai[.]com 25 Apr 2011 A video of Eric Trump 17 Jan 2024, 11:08 UTC dappradars[.]website 25 Apr 2011 A video of Ivanka Trump Not shown Blocked by Bitly as malicious or spam Creation times are from Bitly’s information pages, read on 15 November 2026. Domains are written with brackets so they cannot be clicked. One tweet, three replaced links On 25 April 2011 the account posted three Bitly links to “The Next Generation” videos of Donald Trump Jr., Ivanka Trump and Eric Trump. The first now leads to worldlibertyfinancial-ai[.]com, a domain that borrows the name of World Liberty Financial, the Trump family’s crypto venture. The third leads to dappradars[.]website, one letter away from the crypto analytics site DappRadar, at a path named “eligibility/check”. Bitly blocks the second with a notice that it was “flagged as redirecting to malicious or spam content”. WHOIS records from WhoisXML API show both domains were registered afresh after the links were created. The current registration of dappradars[.]website began at 02:56 UTC on 15 November 2026, through Hostinger, although the Bitly link that points there was created in January 2024. The domain now forwards to a YouTube video. The current registration of worldlibertyfinancial-ai[.]com dates from 11 April 2026, through Namecheap, almost 15 months after the link was created, and its HTTPS certificate failed verification when we checked. We have not seen what either domain served when the links were first made. A replaced link can be replaced again. When the domain behind it lapses, the next buyer inherits whatever traffic the old tweet still sends. More Trump links outside our 97 X users found replaced Bitly links in Trump tweets from 2012 and 2013 that the archive stores only as t.co addresses. We checked two. The link in a tweet of 10 January 2013 was created at 23:52 UTC on 14 November 2026 and opens a page on Steam. The link in a tweet of 10 September 2012 was created at 01:04 UTC on 15 November and opens a YouTube video. Late on 14 November is the earliest change in this wave that we have seen. Which re-created links still work? We ran the same check on the 97 Trump links twice more, at 19:25 and 23:35 UTC on 15 November. The seven links that pointed somewhere new no longer redirect. The other 49 links created years after their tweets still do: 48 were made within 17 minutes of each other on 26 May 2023 and one in February 2025. They point to what look like the original pages, mostly YouTube videos and news articles. We do not know who re-created them or why. The 40 original links work as before. How we counted We used the archive’s condensed yearly files for 2009 to 2016 and found bit.ly links only in tweets up to 2013. From late 2011 Twitter wrapped links in its own t.co shortener, and the archive stores most later links in that form (1,218 of them in 2012), so Bitly links behind those are not among our 97. A link counts as created again when Bitly’s information page shows a creation date more than 30 days after the first tweet that used it. In practice the gap was at least 11 years in every case. Destinations were read from the redirect header without opening the pages. The count covers one account and one link shortener. It shows that these links were claimed. How many of Bitly’s older links can be claimed is something only Bitly can answer. Domain registration data is from WhoisXML API. Who else was affected? CNN reported on the evening of 15 November that old posts from Bill Gates, Justin Trudeau, Mike Pence, the FBI and the US Department of Defense carried redirected Bitly links too, along with a 2013 post from McDonald’s Indonesia account. It counted at least a dozen in Trump’s posts, in a wave that appears limited to posts from 2009 to 2014. Burger King told CNN it had nothing to do with the redirects. We have not checked those links ourselves. Bitly was already disabling affected links when they were reported, and a disabled link no longer shows when it was created. The accounts we verified directly are Burger King, McDonald’s and Donald Trump. What happened on 15 November 2026? The first change we found came late on 14 November. The McDonald’s and Burger King links followed at 05:14 and 05:32 UTC the next morning. All times below are UTC and on 15 November unless stated. How the Bitly link hijacking unfolded Saturday 14 to Sunday 15 November 2026. All times are UTC. Links and domains registered by someone else Posts, statements and our checks 00:00 06:00 12:00 18:00 00:00 Saturday 14 November: the earliest change we found 23:52 Link taken A link in a 2013 Trump tweet is registered and pointed at a page on Steam, the earliest change we found. Sunday 15 November, morning: the brand links are taken 01:04 Link taken A link in a 2012 Trump tweet is registered and pointed at a YouTube video. 02:56 Domain dappradars[.]website, the target of a Trump link replaced in 2024, is registered afresh. 05:14 Link taken The back-half in McDonald’s 2011 tweet is registered and pointed at Wikipedia. 05:32 Link taken The back-half in Burger King’s 2011 tweet is registered and pointed at Wikipedia. 06:51 X An X user quotes the Burger King tweet. The post goes on to pass 2 million views. 07:25 X Another user identifies it as link hijacking and says old Trump posts are affected. 07:49 Link taken A link in a 2009 Trump tweet is registered and pointed at a Roblox profile. 09:18 X A user describes the method in public. 09:36 to 09:57 Links taken Three links in 2010 Trump tweets are registered. Sunday 15 November, afternoon and evening: Bitly responds 13:45 Burger King Burger King’s post shows as unavailable. Its link still redirects to Wikipedia. 14:20 McDonald’s McDonald’s post returns a not-found error. Its link still redirects to Wikipedia too. 15:05 Our check Both links still redirect to Wikipedia. 19:13 Bitly Bitly says on X that an issue let old, inactive links be repurposed, that it has suspended the accounts involved and that it is disabling the affected links. Why it matters: this is the first confirmation from Bitly that old links could be taken over. 19:22 Our check Both links return Bitly’s “Link Deactivated” page. So do six of the seven Trump links in our sample that pointed somewhere new and the two we verified outside it. The seventh shows a warning that the account that created it has been suspended. 21:10 CNN CNN reports redirected links in old posts from Bill Gates, Justin Trudeau, Mike Pence, the FBI and the US Department of Defense. 23:35 Our check Our third check finds no further change. Forty-nine re-created links in the Trump sample still redirect. Status Now The Burger King and McDonald’s links no longer redirect, and neither do the Trump links that pointed somewhere new. Forty-nine re-created links in the Trump sample still work. Bitly has not said how many links were taken. Checked at 23:35 UTC on 15 November. Link creation times are from Bitly’s information pages and post times are from X. Checks are our own. CNN’s report is timed by its publication. Last checked 23:35 UTC, 15 November 2026. Why does a joke link matter? Because the same move works for fraud. The examples from 15 November are pranks: a Wikipedia page, a game profile, a video. The 2025 wave pushed memecoins, and two of the Trump links in our table lead to domains named after crypto services. A link inside an old post from a verified brand, a bank, a ministry or a news outlet carries that account’s credibility, and X shows the post exactly as it was written. Readers have no reason to doubt it. The exposure is wider than X. The same short links sit in old emails, PDFs, slide decks, printed QR codes and help pages. Security researchers file this under broken link hijacking : a link outlives the thing it pointed to, and someone else moves in. What should brands and readers do? Any organisation that posted short links years ago should assume some of them are no longer its own. List the short links in your old posts. Export your post archive from each platform and pull out every bit.ly address. Check each one. Add a plus sign to the link and compare Bitly’s creation date with the date of your post. A later date means the link is no longer yours. Remove what you cannot fix. Delete posts whose links were replaced or no longer resolve, and report replaced links to Bitly. Use a short domain you own for new links , so nobody else can issue the same address. For everyone else, the checks take a few seconds. Do not trust a link because the post is old or the account is verified. The account owner may have no control over where it goes. Preview before you click. Adding a plus sign to a bit.ly link shows the destination without visiting it. Be most careful with pages that ask you to sign in or connect a crypto wallet. What happens next? Bitly has to say whether old back-halves can still be claimed and what it will do about the ones already taken. We found no public statement from Bitly, Burger King or McDonald’s by 14:30 UTC on 15 November. Later that day the links that pointed somewhere new were deactivated, and 49 others created years after their tweets were left working. Bitly confirmed the issue on X at 19:13 UTC and said it was still disabling affected links. Its statement does not say how many links were taken or how. Checks like this one are what our breach verification desk is for, and we will update this article when either company responds or the numbers move. Frequently asked questions Was Burger King hacked in November 2026? No. Nothing was posted from Burger King’s X account. A Bitly short link in a tweet from 24 July 2011 was registered again by someone else on 15 November 2026, so the old tweet began sending readers to a different page. Was McDonald’s hacked? No. A Bitly link in a McDonald’s tweet from 7 June 2011 was registered again at 05:14 UTC on 15 November 2026 and pointed at Wikipedia’s article on the September 11 attacks. Nothing was posted from the McDonald’s account. Why did a Burger King tweet link to a list of Nazi concentration camps? The tweet’s Bitly link, bit[.]ly/19BFiM, originally advertised a restaurant locator. Bitly’s information page shows the link was created again at 05:32 UTC on 15 November 2026 with a Wikipedia article as its destination. Burger King did not choose that destination. What is Bitly link hijacking? It is when someone registers the ending of an old Bitly link that no longer exists and points it at a page of their choice. Every old post, email or document that carries the link then leads to the new destination. No account is broken into. How can I tell whether a Bitly link has been replaced? Add a plus sign to the end of the link. Bitly shows the destination and the date the link was created. If the creation date is later than the post or document the link appears in, the link is not the original. Were Donald Trump’s old tweets hacked? No. Ransomnews checked 97 Bitly links in tweets from 2009 to 2013. Fifty-six were created again after the tweets were posted and one is blocked by Bitly. Seven of them lead to destinations unrelated to the tweets, including two domains that copy the names of crypto services. Has Bitly fixed the problem? A fix was reported in February 2025 after links in Trump posts were pointed at memecoin pages. Links created on 15 November 2026 show that old endings can be claimed now. Bitly had made no public statement that we could find by 14:30 UTC that day. It confirmed the issue on X at 19:13 UTC and said it was disabling the affected links. It added that its Trust and Safety team is working on protections against similar misuse. Who else was affected by the Bitly link hijacking? CNN reported redirected Bitly links in old posts from Bill Gates, Justin Trudeau, Mike Pence, the FBI and the US Department of Defense, as well as Burger King, McDonald’s and Donald Trump. Ransomnews verified the Burger King, McDonald’s and Trump links directly. Are the hijacked Bitly links still active? The ones we tracked are not. By 19:22 UTC on 15 November 2026 the Burger King and McDonald’s links, and the Trump links that pointed somewhere new, returned Bitly’s “Link Deactivated” page. Bitly said it was still disabling affected links, so check any old short link before you trust it. title: Protomaps: Self-hosting map tiles has gotten cheap and easy
body_text: Protomaps: Self-hosting map tiles has gotten cheap and easy â Bruce RÃ¶ttgers Bruce RÃ¶ttgers about // portfolio // blog blog // dev // projects Protomaps: Self-hosting map tiles has gotten cheap and easy PMTiles is a tile format which works via HTTP Range requests and can be deployed as a single file to a storage bucket. 2026-11-15 // 4 min read // contents 1 Getting some Maps 2 Deploying to Bunny.net 3 Embedding the Map Â· Notes // contents 1 Getting some Maps 2 Deploying to Bunny.net 3 Embedding the Map Â· Notes I came across Protomaps in research for my latest project, Mapboard . 1 For most non-commercial projects, commercial APIs become prohibitively expensive if you ever go viral (Mapbox, for instance, charges $5 per 1k map loads once youâve exhausted the free tier). PMTiles, part of the Protomaps ecosystem, is a tile format that ships in a single file, accessible via Range requests, and is thus extremely portable and easy to deploy. For CDNs that support caching Range requests of large files, it requires no effort besides down- and uploading it to storage. For others, like Cloudflare, you can utilize an edge function to translate between the traditional x/y/z URL path and Range requests. Getting some Maps If all you want is the world map, getting it is as simple as going to the build page and downloading the latest daily build. However, more fun can be had with the CLI . For example, you can extract data for only a bounding box or specific zoom levels, to get a significantly smaller file. Deploying to Bunny.net One great CDN for deploying this is Bunny.net (affiliate link) . They support HTTP Range requests, donât collect personal data by default, 2 are headquartered in the EU, and offer low-cost access to a global network of CDN and edge storage servers. Pricing varies based on region and replication factor of the edge storage. But generally you pay $0.01/GB ($0.005/GB on the smaller Volume network) for bandwidth to Europe and North America, and $0.01/GB/month (no replication) to $0.055/GB/month (maximum replication) for storage. A high degree of replication mostly matters for latency in case of a cache miss (as the data is further replicated when itâs cached at the CDN PoPs). In practical terms, storing the 139GB world map with replication to most continents (5x) will run you about $5/month in storage fees. Loading a map of Europe on a laptop and zooming in on a city causes about 5MB of data to be transmitted, which would be $0.00005 â further navigations and reloads will be less expensive as more of the map gets cached locally. At $0.05/1k map loads that could be 100x cheaper than Mapbox. However, the actual bandwidth of course varies (less for people that bounce immediately, possibly tens of MB for heavy users). For Mapbox you only pay a flat fee per visit. Uploading the file Itâs a good idea to create a storage zone with S3 compatibility enabled, as uploading via the HTTP API timed out after 15 minutes for me. Then, with rclone installed, you can download and stream the file to the Bunny storage zone. Preferably in tmux or from a temporary VPS, if your connection isnât great. rclone config create bunnycdn s3 \ provider=Other \ access_key_id="<zone-name>" \ secret_access_key="<storage-key>" \ endpoint="https://<primary-region>-s3.storage.bunnycdn.com" rclone copyurl "<build-url>" "bunnycdn:<zone-name>/<filename>.pmtiles" \ --s3-chunk-size 256M \ --progress Configuring the pull zone Theoretically, at this point you just need to create a pull zone, select the storage zone as an origin, and youâre done. Practically, it would be sensible to change some settings. Allowed CORS origins can be configured under Security > General > Allowed referrers, so that other websites cannot embed your tiles. Youâll also want to verify under Caching that âOptimize for large object deliveryâ is enabled, as this makes it possible to cache Range requests. You might also want to dissuade people from downloading the whole file and leaving you with a large CDN bill. The most practical way Iâve found for this is limiting the download speed to 10kB/s after 10MB transmitted in a single request (using the âDownload speed limitsâ and âLimit afterâ settings under âNetwork limitsâ). Regular usage should never reach this amount. You may further want to introduce a requests/second limit (do note that legitimate usage can also quickly reach high numbers here) or a monthly bandwidth limit for the pull zone. Embedding the Map With the tiles deployed, the only thing left to do is to embed them in your website via MapLibre GL, for example. To do this, youâll need to install the pmtiles npm package and add the protocol and a style to MapLibre as detailed in the official installation guide . Congratulations, you now host your own cost-effective and highly available map of the world! // notes (2) Basically, Excalidraw but on a map for travel planning. Launch post coming soon. â The last octet of IP addresses is dropped. If you transmit personal data via the CDN, that is of course still processed. â // newsletter Stay updated on new blog posts and projects by me; sent less than once per week. subscribe â // written by Hi, Iâm Bruce, a Computer Science student at ETH Zurich. I build mobile apps, websites and other products, and I write about the interesting things I run into along the way. More about me â github // email // rss // letters reply by email â Please send an email if you wish to comment on this post. I will share select replies here with the author's permission. Also discussed on Hacker News âï¸ Â© 2026 Bruce RÃ¶ttgers theme: auto // light // dark github // email // rss

title: Microsoft 365 outage leads to chlorine gas poisoning of 15 hotel guests
body_text: Phantasialand: Chlorunfall nach Microsoft-Panne zum Inhalt zur Navigation zur Suche Wetter Verkehr Menü öffnen Menü schließen Suche einblenden Suche ausblenden Eingabe löschen Suchen Mein NRW Übersicht Mein NRW Aachen und Eifel Bergisches Land Münsterland Niederrhein Ostwestfalen-Lippe Rheinland Ruhrgebiet Sauer- und Siegerland Politik Wirtschaft Sport Freizeit Kultur Wetter Verkehr ARD Mediathek ARD Sounds Hier findest du uns auch Mein NRW Übersicht Mein NRW Aachen und Eifel Bergisches Land Münsterland Niederrhein Ostwestfalen-Lippe Rheinland Ruhrgebiet Sauer- und Siegerland Politik Wirtschaft Sport Freizeit Kultur Wetter Verkehr ARD Mediathek ARD Sounds Suche einblenden Suche ausblenden Eingabe löschen Suchen Sie befinden sich hier: WDR Mein NRW Rheinland Rhein-Erft-Kreis Video starten, abbrechen mit Escape IT-Panne Schuld für Chlorgasunfall im Phantasialand | WDR aktuell Bildquelle: WDR WDR . 46 Sek. . Verfügbar bis 15.11.2028 . Nach IT-Störung bei Microsoft : 15 Gäste verletzt nach Chlorunfall im Phantasialand Stand: 16.11.2026, 19:15 Uhr Wegen der Microsoft-Störung am Freitag bekam das Phantasialand nicht mit, dass zu viel Chlor im Pool war. 15 Gäste wurden verletzt. Ein Cybersecurity-Architekt sieht den Fehler beim Freizeitpark, nicht bei Microsoft. Von Caroline Jüngermann , Friederike Müllender , Lara Burghardt und Martin Heuchel Diesem Problem waren wir alle ausgesetzt: Am Freitag gab es eine Störung, die den US-Softwarekonzern Microsoft lahmgelegt hat. Unter anderem das E-Mail-Programm Outlook. Betroffen war auch das Phantasialand. Durch die Störung kamen keine Mails an, wie das Unternehmen dem WDR am Samstag mitteilte. So bekam niemand mit, dass das Wartungssicherheitssystem der Saunalandschaft längst per Mail Alarm geschlagen hat. Denn das automatischen Dosiersystem hatte zu viel Chlor in den Pool gepumpt. Reizungen der Atemwege Dadurch wurden Gäste im Hotel Ling Bao des Phantasialands in Brühl verletzt. Sie haben über gesundheitliche Probleme geklagt, nachdem sie den Pool besucht hatten. Der wurde zeitweise gesperrt, konnte inzwischen aber wieder freigegeben werden, wie die Feuerwehr am Samstag dem WDR mitteilte. Wegen der Beschwerden der Hotel-Besucher wurden Rettungskräfte und die Feuerwehr gerufen. 13 Gäste klagten über Reizungen der Atemwege, letztlich stieg die Zahl der Betroffenen auf insgesamt 15. Überhöhter Chlorgehalt: Eine Person bleibt im Krankenhaus Zunächst hieß es, dass fünf Gäste ins Krankenhaus gebracht wurden, später wurde die Zahl auf vier korrigiert, eine Person davon blieb wegen einer mittelschweren Verletzung zur Beobachtung im Krankenhaus. Im Hotel ergaben Tests der Einsatzkräfte einen Defekt des automatischen Dosiersystems für den Pool. Dies hatte zu einem deutlich überhöhten Chlorgehalt geführt. Das Wasser wurde daher ausgetauscht. Betreiber der Mauritius-Therme wird hellhörig Die Nachricht über den Chlorunfall im Hotel im Phantasialand hat auch Max Wiesen, den Betreiber von "Mauritius Hotel und Therme", hellhörig werden lassen. "Da denkt man natürlich immer selber: Oh je, kann uns das auch passieren?" Max Wiesen, Betreiber von "Mauritius Hotel und Therme" Betreiber Max Wiese und Haustechniker Ingo Braun. Bildquelle: WDR/Friederike Müllender Das Erste was er dann gemacht habe, sei, mit seiner Technik zu sprechen, " wie wir da abgesichert sind. " Ansprechpartner für ihn ist sein Kollege Ingo Braun. Er ist bereits seit 15 Jahren Haustechniker und kennt sich mit den Pools aus. Der Wasserwert werde dreimal am Tag gemessen, sagt Braun. " Und wir haben ein Alarmsystem. Wenn in einem Pool etwas passiert, eine Überchlorung oder eine Unterchlorung, dann geht eine rote Lampe an, dass jeder Bescheid weiß. " Cybersecurity-Architekt sieht Fehler bei Phantasialand Auch Cybersecurity-Architekt und Informatiker Stephan Skrobisch hat den Fall im Phantasialand verfolgt, für ihn ist die Firma Microsoft nicht für den Vorfall verantwortlich. " Es ist ganz klar die Einrichtung der Anlage. Es wurde versäumt, einen weiteren Meldemechanismus zu implementieren ". Das könnte zum Beispiel ein akustisches Signal sein. Ein Warnsystem, das Menschen schützen soll, dürfe nicht allein von einem E-Mail-Postfach abhängen. Verletzungen durch Chlorgas im Phantasialand WDR . 14.11.2026 . 36 Sek. . Verfügbar bis 13.11.2028 .
